summaries.Good news: Today brings stories of resilience and discovery: a baby thriving on an artificial heart while awaiting transplant, a teen's fungal breakthrough for ocean cleanup, and beavers becoming nature's architects in ecosystem restoration.
summaries.Ideas: Leaders and organizations are rethinking fundamentals—from how AI should be questioned to how workplace culture can better serve human performance, while new tools are democratizing skills from web design to customer feedback.
summaries.Technology: The innovation landscape spans from Europe's first commercial orbital rocket and recyclable airplane materials to intimate gadgets like privacy-focused foldable phones and pocket-sized e-readers, while broader questions emerge about memory costs and copyright in the AI era.
summaries.Design: Design's economic and cultural impact is surging—the UK industry now contributes £136.7B annually—while architects and makers are pioneering bold new materials like volcanic rock exoskeletons and transforming derelict spaces into vibrant community bathhouses.

items.title: Groupwork completes "world-first" high-rise held up by stone exoskeleton
items.snippet: A thousand tons of volcanic rock replace concrete and steel in Petra Heights, a housing development in north London by architecture studio Groupwork and engineer Webb Yates. items.line: A volcanic rock exoskeleton replacing concrete and steel demonstrates that radical material innovation can be both structurally sound and environmentally transformative.

items.title: Badweather converts derelict canal boat into London's first off-grid bathhouse
items.snippet: Architecture collective Badweather has transformed a 17-metre canal boat into Soak, an off-grid bathhouse that moves to a new location along London's waterways every two weeks. Soak combines a wood-fired sauna, two cold plunge pools, showers, changing facilities and a small bar for up to 12 people.
items.line: Converting a canal boat into London's first mobile off-grid bathhouse shows how constraint and resourcefulness can create genuinely new community experiences.

items.line: A solid-state cooler that uses heat to generate cold opens unexpected pathways for processor efficiency and challenges our intuitions about thermodynamics.

items.title: Beavers Are Having a Moment
items.snippet: Over the last 20 years, Oregon’s wilderness has suffered big time. Salmon have disappeared, wildfires have scoured the hills and drought has parched once-fertile soils. Years of small fixes — a little forest thinning here, a little fish-ladder installation there — have helped, but not nearly enough
items.line: Beavers restoring Oregon's drought-damaged wilderness, salmon, and soils shows that nature's own architects often outperform human intervention—a humbling ecological win.
